value.zh: 韓襃 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 梁昕 皇甫璠 辛慶之 王子直 杜杲 呂思禮 徐招 檀翥 孟信 宗懍 劉璠 柳遐

value.literal: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, Liu Xia

value.zh: 劉璠，字寶義，沛人也。
value.en: Liu Fan, whose style name was Baoyi, came from Pei.
value.literal: Liu Fan, style name Baoyi, was a native of Pei.

value.zh: 六世祖敏，以永嘉亂，徙居廣陵。
value.en: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, fleeing the chaos of the Yongjia era, moved the family to Guangling.
value.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, because of the Yongjia chaos, moved to settle in Guangling.

value.zh: 父臧，性方正，篤志好學，居家以孝聞。
value.en: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted to learning, and renowned at home for filial conduct.
value.literal: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted in will and fond of learning, and at home was known for filial conduct.

value.zh: 仕梁，為著作郎。
value.en: Under Liang he served as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
value.literal: He served Liang as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 璠九歲而孤，居喪合禮。
value.en: Fan lost his father at nine and observed mourning in full accordance with ritual.
value.literal: Fan at nine years lost his father and observed mourning in accordance with ritual.

value.zh: 少好讀書，兼善文筆。
value.en: From youth he loved books and was also skilled with the brush.
value.literal: In youth he loved reading and was also skilled in literary composition.

value.zh: 十七，為上黃侯蕭曄所器重。
value.en: At seventeen he won the deep esteem of the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.
value.literal: At seventeen he was deeply valued by the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.

value.zh: 范陽張綰，梁之外戚，才高口辯，見推於世。
value.en: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, a Liang imperial in-law, was talented and eloquent and widely admired.
value.literal: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, an in-law of Liang, was talented and eloquent and was praised by the age.

value.zh: 以曄懿貴，亦假借之。
value.en: Because Ye was of high rank and noble birth, Wan also relied on his patronage.
value.literal: Because Ye was honored and noble, Wan also leaned on him.

value.zh: 璠年少未仕，而負才使氣，不為之屈。
value.en: Fan was still young and had not yet entered office, yet trusting in his talent and proud in spirit, he would not defer to Wan.
value.literal: Fan was young and had not yet taken office, yet relied on his talent and was proud in spirit, and would not yield to Wan.

value.zh: 綰嘗于新渝侯宅，因酒後詬京兆杜杲曰：「寒士不遜。」
value.en: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after drinking, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao: "A poor scholar knows no deference".
value.literal: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after wine, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao, saying: "A poor scholar shows no deference".

value.zh: 璠厲色曰：「此坐誰非寒士？」
value.en: Fan said sharply, "Who at this table is not a poor scholar?"
value.literal: Fan said sternly: "Who at this gathering is not a poor scholar?"

value.zh: 璠本意在綰，而曄以為屬己，辭色不平。
value.en: Fan's remark was really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought it was meant for him and showed his displeasure.
value.literal: Fan's words were really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought they were directed at himself and showed displeasure in face and speech.

value.zh: 璠曰：「何王之門不可曳長裾也！」
value.en: Fan said, "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!
value.literal: Fan said: "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!

value.zh: 遂拂衣而去。
value.en: With that he shook out his robes and walked away.
value.literal: Then he shook out his robes and left.

value.zh: 曄謝之，乃止。
value.en: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan relent.
value.literal: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan stop.

value.zh: 後隨曄在淮南。
value.en: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.
value.literal: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.

value.zh: 璠母在建康遘疾，璠弗之知。
value.en: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, but Fan knew nothing of it.
value.literal: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, and Fan did not know of it.

value.zh: 嘗忽一日舉身楚痛，尋而家信至，雲其母病。
value.en: One day his whole body was suddenly racked with pain; soon afterward a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.
value.literal: Suddenly one day his whole body was racked with pain; soon a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.

value.zh: 璠即號泣戒道，絕而又蘇。
value.en: Fan at once wailed and set out on the road; he stopped breathing and revived.
value.literal: Fan at once wailed and prepared to travel; he stopped breathing and revived.

value.zh: 當身痛之辰，即母死之日。
value.en: The day his body was racked with pain was exactly the day his mother died.
value.literal: The day his body was in pain was exactly the day his mother died.

value.zh: 居喪毀瘠，遂感風氣，服闋後一年，猶杖而後起。
value.en: In mourning he wasted away and then contracted a wind ailment; even a year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff to rise.
value.literal: In mourning he wasted away; he then contracted wind illness, and a full year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff before he could rise.

value.zh: 及曄終於毗陵，故吏多分散，璠獨奉曄喪還都，墳成乃退。
value.en: When Ye died at Piling, many of his former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted the coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was finished.
value.literal: When Ye died at Piling, many former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted Ye's coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was completed.

value.zh: 梁簡文暼寺在東宮，遇曄素重，諸不送者多被劾責，唯璠獨被優嘗賞。
value.en: When Jianwen of Liang was crown prince at the Eastern Palace, Ye had long been held in high esteem, and many who failed to attend his funeral were impeached and punished; Fan alone received special commendation and reward.
value.literal: When Jianwen of Liang was at the Eastern Palace, since Ye had long been held in esteem, many who did not attend the funeral were impeached and punished, but Fan alone received special commendation and reward.

value.zh: 解褐王國常侍，非其好也。
value.en: On first taking office he became Regular Attendant of a princely domain, a post that did not suit him.
value.literal: On first appointment he became Regular Attendant of the princely domain, which was not to his liking.

value.zh: 璠少慷慨，好功名，志欲立事邊城，不樂隨牒平進。
value.en: From youth Fan was generous and hungered for fame and achievement; he wished to make his mark on the frontier and took no pleasure in routine promotion.
value.literal: Fan from youth was generous and fond of fame and merit, resolved to achieve deeds on the frontier, and did not delight in advancing step by step through routine appointments.

value.zh: 曾宜豐侯蕭脩出為北徐州刺史，即請為其輕車府主簿，兼記室參軍。
value.en: When the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, was appointed Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.
value.literal: Once when the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, went out as Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.

value.zh: 脩為梁州，又板為中記室，補華陽太守。
value.en: When Xiu became Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and made Administrator of Huayang.
value.literal: When Xiu was made Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and supplemented as Administrator of Huayang.

value.zh: 屬侯景度江，梁室大亂，脩以璠有才略，甚親委之。
value.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into chaos, Xiu, recognizing Fan's talent and strategic mind, entrusted him with great confidence.
value.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into great disorder, Xiu, because Fan had talent and strategy, entrusted him with great intimacy.

value.zh: 時寇難繁興，未有所定，璠乃喟然賦詩以見志。
value.en: Raids and troubles arose on every side and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to declare his resolve.
value.literal: At that time raids and troubles arose in profusion and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to express his resolve.

value.zh: 其末章曰：「隨會平王室，夷吾匡霸功。
value.en: Its final stanza reads: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.
value.literal: Its final stanza says: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.

value.zh: 虛薄而時用，徒然慕昔風。」
value.en: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the heroes of old".
value.literal: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the winds of old".

value.zh: 脩開府，置佐史，以璠為諮議參軍，仍領記室。
value.en: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and appointed aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.
value.literal: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and established aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.

value.zh: 梁元帝承制，授樹功將軍、鎮西府諮議參軍。
value.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.
value.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.

value.zh: 賜書曰：「鄧禹文學，尚或執戈；
value.en: An imperial letter said, "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;
value.literal: An imperial letter said: "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;

value.zh: 葛洪書生，且雲破賊。
value.en: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.
value.literal: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.

value.zh: 前修無遠，屬望良深。」
value.en: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you run very deep".
value.literal: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you are deep indeed".

value.zh: 元帝尋以脩紹鄱陽之封，且為雍州刺史，復以璠為為脩平北府司馬。
value.en: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.
value.literal: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan as Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.

value.zh: 及武陵王紀稱制於蜀，以璠為中書侍郎。
value.en: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.
value.literal: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 遣召璠，使者八反，乃至蜀。
value.en: Ji sent to summon Fan; the envoy returned eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.
value.literal: He sent to summon Fan; the envoy came back eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.

value.zh: 又以為黃門侍郎，令長史劉孝勝深布心腹，使工畫《陳平度河歸漢圖》以遺之。
value.en: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted agents deeply; he also had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" and sent it to Fan as a gift.
value.literal: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted men deeply and had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" as a gift to him.

value.zh: 璠苦求還，中記室韋登私曰：「殿下忍而蓄憾，足下不留，將致大禍。
value.en: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately, "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will follow. If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine?
value.literal: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately: "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will come. If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine?

value.zh: 脫使盜遮於葭萌，則卿殆矣。
value.en: If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished.
value.literal: If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished.

value.zh: 孰若共構大廈，使身名俱美哉！」
value.en: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine"?
value.literal: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine"?

value.zh: 璠正色曰：「卿欲緩頰於我邪？
value.en: Fan said sternly, "Do you wish to soften my resolve?
value.literal: Fan said sternly: "Do you wish to soften my resolve?

value.zh: 我與府侯分義已定，豈以寵辱夷險易其心乎！
value.en: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?
value.literal: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?

value.zh: 丈夫立志，當死生以之耳。
value.en: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.
value.literal: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.

value.zh: 殿下方布大義於天下，終不逞志於一人。」
value.en: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."
value.literal: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."

value.zh: 紀知不為己用，乃厚贈而遣之。
value.en: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.
value.literal: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.

value.zh: 臨別，紀又解其佩刀贈璠曰：「想見物思人。」
value.en: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying, "When you see this object, think of the man".
value.literal: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying: "When you see this object, think of the man".

value.zh: 璠曰：「敢不奉揚威靈，克翦奸宄。」
value.en: Fan said, "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"
value.literal: Fan said: "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"

value.zh: 紀於是遣使拜脩為益州刺史，封隨郡王，以璠為府長史，加蜀郡太守。
value.en: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.
value.literal: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.

value.zh: 還至白馬西，屬達奚武軍已至南鄭，璠不得入城，遂降武。
value.en: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng; Fan could not enter the city and surrendered to Wu.
value.literal: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng, and Fan could not enter the city, so he surrendered to Wu.

value.zh: 周文帝素聞其名，先戒武曰：「勿使劉璠死。」
value.en: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu: "Do not let Liu Fan die".
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu, saying: "Do not let Liu Fan die".

value.zh: 故武先令璠赴闕。
value.en: Therefore Wu first sent Fan to the capital.
value.literal: Therefore Wu first had Fan go to the capital.

value.zh: 周文見之如舊，謂僕射申徽曰：「劉璠佳士，古人何以過之！」
value.en: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui, "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!
value.literal: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui: "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!

value.zh: 徽曰：「晉人滅吳，利在二陸。
value.en: Hui said, "When the Jin destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.
value.literal: Hui said: "When the Jin people destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.

value.zh: 明公今平梁漢，得劉璠也。」
value.en: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."
value.literal: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."

value.zh: 時南鄭尚拒守，達奚武請屠之，周文將許焉，唯令全脩一家而已。
value.en: Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu asked to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.
value.literal: At that time Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu requested to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.

value.zh: 璠乃請之于朝，周文怒而不許也。
value.en: Fan then pleaded at court, but Emperor Wen was angry and refused.
value.literal: Fan then pleaded at court; Emperor Wen was angry and would not consent.

value.zh: 璠泣而固請，移時不退。
value.en: Fan wept and pleaded firmly, and for a long time would not withdraw.
value.literal: Fan wept and firmly pleaded, and for a long time would not withdraw.

value.zh: 柳仲禮侍側，曰：「此烈士也。」
value.en: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said, "This is a man of heroic resolve".
value.literal: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said: "This is a man of heroic resolve".

value.zh: 周文既納蕭脩降，又許其反國。
value.en: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.
value.literal: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.

value.zh: 脩至長安累月，未之遣也。
value.en: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.
value.literal: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.

value.zh: 璠因侍宴，周文曰：「我于古誰比？」
value.en: While attending a banquet, Fan was asked by Emperor Wen, "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?
value.literal: Fan, while attending a banquet, was asked by Emperor Wen: "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?

value.zh: 曰：「常以公命世英主，湯、武莫逮。
value.en: He said, "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.
value.literal: He said: "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.

value.zh: 今日所見，曾是齊桓、晉文之不若。」
value.en: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."
value.literal: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."

value.zh: 周文曰：「我不得比湯、武，望與伊、周為匹，何桓、文之不若乎？」
value.en: Emperor Wen said, "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to stand equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why should I fall short of Huan and Wen?"
value.literal: Emperor Wen said: "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to be the equal of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why fall short of Huan and Wen?"

value.zh: 對曰：「齊桓存三亡國，晉文不失信于伐原。」
value.en: He replied, "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."
value.literal: He replied: "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."

value.zh: 語未終，周文撫掌曰：「我解爾意，欲激我耳。」
value.en: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said, "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."
value.literal: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said: "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."

value.zh: 即命遣脩。
value.en: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.
value.literal: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.

value.zh: 脩請與璠俱還，周文不許。
value.en: Xiu asked to return together with Fan, but Emperor Wen refused.
value.literal: Xiu asked to return together with Fan; Emperor Wen would not consent.

value.zh: 以璠為中外府記室，遷黃門侍郎、儀同三司。
value.en: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.
value.literal: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.

value.zh: 嘗臥疾居家，對雪興感，乃作《雪賦》以遂志焉。
value.en: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.
value.literal: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.

value.zh: 初，蕭脩在漢中與蕭紀箋，及答西魏書、移襄陽文，皆璠辭也。
value.en: When Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji, his replies to Western Wei, and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all written by Fan.
value.literal: At first, when Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji and his replies to Western Wei's letters and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all Fan's compositions.

value.zh: 儒林下
value.en: Confucian Scholars, Part Two
value.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.

value.zh: 何妥，字棲風，西城人也。
value.en: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, came from Xicheng.
value.literal: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, was a native of Xicheng.

value.zh: 父細腳胡，通商入蜀，遂家郫縣。
value.en: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.
value.literal: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.

value.zh: 事梁武陵王紀，主知金帛，因致巨富，號為西州大賈。
value.en: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.
value.literal: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.

value.zh: 妥少機警，八歲游國子學，助教顧良戲之曰：「汝姓何，是荷葉之荷？
value.en: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and Assistant Instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?
value.literal: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and the assistant instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?

value.zh: 為河水之河？」
value.en: Or the he of river water?"
value.literal: Or the he of river water?"

value.zh: 妥應聲答曰：「先生姓顧，是眷顧之顧？
value.en: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?
value.literal: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?

value.zh: 為新故之故？」
value.en: Or the gu of old and new?"
value.literal: Or the gu of old and new?"

value.zh: 眾咸異之。
value.en: The crowd all marveled at him.
value.literal: The crowd all marveled at him.

value.zh: 十七，以伎巧事湘東王。
value.en: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.
value.literal: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.

value.zh: 後知其聰明，召為誦書左右。
value.en: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.
value.literal: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.

value.zh: 時蘭陵蕭翽，亦有俊才，住青楊巷，妥住白楊頭。
value.en: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo at White Poplar Head.
value.literal: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo lived at White Poplar Head.

value.zh: 時人為之語曰：「世有兩俊，白楊何妥，青楊蕭翽。」
value.en: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar."
value.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar."

value.zh: 其見美如此。
value.en: Thus was he admired.
value.literal: Thus was he admired.

value.zh: 陳書卷三十一
value.en: Book of Chen, Volume 31
value.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 31

value.zh: 猛字智武，毅之弟也。
value.en: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.

value.zh: 幼俶儻，有幹略。
value.en: In youth he was bold and unconventional, with capacity and stratagem.
value.literal: In youth he was bold and unconventional and had capacity and stratagem.

value.zh: 既壯，便弓馬，膽氣過人。
value.en: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.
value.literal: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.

value.zh: 青溪之戰，猛自旦訖暮，與虜短兵接，殺傷甚眾。
value.en: At Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.
value.literal: In the battle at Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.

value.zh: 臺城陷，隨兄毅西上京，累戰功為威戎將軍。
value.en: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital and by accumulated battle merit became might-of-armies general.
value.literal: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital; by accumulated battle merit he became Might-of-Armies General.

value.zh: 梁
value.en: Liang
value.literal: Liang

value.en: Collation variant: (An).
value.literal: (An).

value.zh: 南安侯蕭方矩為湘州刺史，〔一０〕以猛為司馬。
value.en: Southern An marquis Xiao Fangju was made inspector of Xiangzhou [10], and Meng was made marshal of the staff.
value.literal: Southern An Marquis Xiao Fangju was made Inspector of Xiangzhou, and Meng was made Marshal of the Staff.

value.zh: 會武陵王蕭紀舉兵自漢江東下，方矩遣猛率湘、郢之卒，隨都督陸法和進軍以拒之。
value.en: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following area commander Lu Fahe to resist him.
value.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following Area Commander Lu Fahe in an advance to resist him.

value.zh: 時紀已下，樓船戰艦據巴江，爭峽口，相持久之，不能決。
value.en: Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth in a long stalemate that could not be decided.
value.literal: At the time Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth; they faced each other for a long stalemate and could not decide it.

value.zh: 法和揣紀師老卒墯，因令猛率驍勇三千，輕舸百餘乘，衝流直上，出其不意，鼓譟薄之。
value.en: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack and ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats straight upstream, taking him unawares with drums and clamor pressing close.
value.literal: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack; he therefore ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats upstream straight up, taking him unawares, with drums and clamor pressing close.

value.zh: 紀眾倉卒驚駭，不及整列，皆棄艦登岸，赴水死者以千數。
value.en: Ji's host was startled in haste and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.
value.literal: Ji's host in haste was startled and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.

value.zh: 時紀心膂數百人，猶在左右，猛將部曲三十餘人，蒙楯橫戈，直登紀舟，瞋目大呼，紀侍衛皆披靡，相枕藉不敢動。
value.en: Several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side. Meng led more than thirty private troops, shields up and spears level, straight onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.
value.literal: At the time several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side; Meng led more than thirty men of his private troops, shielded and spear in hand, straight up onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants all scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.

value.zh: 猛手擒紀父子三人，斬於舟中，盡收其船艦器械。
value.en: Meng seized Ji and his father and son—three men—and beheaded them in the boat, and gathered all their ships and equipment.
value.literal: Meng with his own hand seized Ji and his father and son, three men, and beheaded them in the boat; he gathered all their ships and equipment.

value.zh: 以功授游騎將軍，封安山縣伯，邑一千戶。
value.en: For merit he was made roaming-cavalry general and enfeoffed as baron of Anshan county with a fief of one thousand households.
value.literal: For merit he was made Roaming-Cavalry General and enfeoffed as Baron of Anshan County with a fief of one thousand households.

value.zh: 仍進軍撫定梁、益，蜀境悉平。
value.en: He still advanced to pacify Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.
value.literal: He still advanced to pacify and settle Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.

value.zh: 軍還，遷持節、散騎常侍、輕車將軍、司州刺史，進爵為侯，增邑并前二千戶。
value.en: When the army returned he was made bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, light-carriage general, and inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced to marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.
value.literal: When the army returned he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Light-Carriage General, and Inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced in rank to Marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 梁書卷第四十一 列傳第三十五
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35

value.zh: 第五弟孝勝，歷官邵陵王法曹、湘東王安西主簿記室、尚書左丞。
value.en: His fifth brother Xiaosheng served as law aide to the Prince of Shaoling, recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifier of the West, and Left Assistant in the Secretariat.
value.literal: His fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held office as law aide to the Prince of Shaoling, recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifier of the West, and Left Assistant in the Secretariat.

value.zh: 出爲信義太守，公事免。
value.en: He was sent out as administrator of Xinyi and removed for a disciplinary offense.
value.literal: He went out as administrator of Xinyi and was dismissed for an official offense.

value.zh: 久之，復爲尚書右丞，兼散騎常侍。
value.en: Long afterward he again became Right Assistant in the Secretariat and concurrently regular palace attendant.
value.literal: After a long interval he again became Right Assistant in the Secretariat and concurrently regular palace attendant.

value.zh: 聘魏還，爲安西武陵王紀長史、蜀郡太守。
value.en: Back from an embassy to Wei he was chief clerk to Prince Ji of Wuling, Pacifier of the West, and administrator of Shujun.
value.literal: On return from an embassy to Wei he became chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling of the Pacifier of the West, Ji, and administrator of Shujun.

value.zh: 太清中，侯景陷京師，紀僭號於蜀，以孝勝爲尚書僕射。
value.en: During Great Clarity, after Hou Jing seized the capital, Ji set himself up in Shu and made Xiaosheng Minister of the Left.
value.literal: In the Great Clarity era, when Hou Jing took the capital, Ji declared himself emperor in Shu and made Xiaosheng Minister of the Left.

value.zh: 承聖中，隨紀出峽口，兵敗，被執下獄。
value.en: In the Chengsheng period he followed Ji through the gorge; defeated, he was taken and cast into prison.
value.literal: In the Chengsheng era he followed Ji out through the gorge; the army was defeated and he was seized and thrown into prison.

value.zh: 世祖尋宥之，起爲司徒右長史。
value.en: The Founding Emperor soon forgave him and made him right chief clerk of the Secretariat.
value.literal: The Founding Emperor soon pardoned him and raised him to right chief clerk of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 第七弟孝先，武陵王法曹、主簿。
value.en: His seventh brother Xiaoxian was law aide and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling.
value.literal: His seventh younger brother Xiaoxian served as law aide and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling.

value.zh: 王遷益州，隨府轉安西記室。
value.en: When the prince moved to Yizhou, he followed the staff and became recorder to the Pacifier of the West.
value.literal: When the prince was transferred to Yizhou, he followed the prince's staff and became recorder to the Pacifier of the West.

value.zh: 承聖中，與兄孝勝俱隨紀軍出峽口，兵敗，至江陵，世祖以爲黃門侍郎，遷侍中。
value.en: In Chengsheng he and Xiaosheng both followed Ji's army through the gorge; beaten, they came to Jiangling, and the Founding Emperor made Xiaoxian Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, then palace attendant.
value.literal: In the Chengsheng era he and his brother Xiaosheng both followed Ji's army out through the gorge; defeated, they reached Jiangling, and the Founding Emperor made Xiaoxian Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and promoted him to palace attendant.

value.zh: 兄弟並善五言詩，見重於世。
value.en: All the brothers excelled at five-character poetry and were held in honor by their age.
value.literal: The brothers were all skilled at five-character verse and were esteemed in the world.

value.zh: 文集值亂，今不具存。
value.en: Their collections were destroyed in the chaos and no longer survive whole.
value.literal: Their collected writings were lost in the disorders and are not fully preserved today.

value.zh: 蕭幾字德玄，齊曲江公遙欣子也。
value.en: Xiao Ji, styled Dexuan, was the son of Duke Yaoxin of Qujiang under Qi.
value.literal: Xiao Ji, courtesy name Dexuan, was son of the Duke of Qujiang, Yaoxin, of Qi.

value.zh: 年十歲，能屬文。
value.en: At ten he could already write prose.
value.literal: At ten he could compose literary pieces.

value.zh: 早孤，有弟九人，並皆稚小，幾恩愛篤睦，聞於朝野。
value.en: Fatherless while young, he had nine younger brothers, all infants; Ji's love among them was warm and close, and word of it reached court and countryside.
value.literal: Orphaned early, he had nine younger brothers, all still very young; Ji's affection among them was deep and harmonious, and the court and common people heard of it.

value.zh: 性溫和，與物無競，清貧自立。
value.en: Gentle by nature, he strove with no one and lived upright in honest poverty.
value.literal: His nature was mild and gentle; he did not contend with others and upheld himself in clean poverty.

value.zh: 好學，善草隸書。
value.en: He loved study and wrote well in cursive and clerical hands.
value.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at cursive and clerical script.

value.zh: 湘州刺史楊公則，曲江之故吏也。
value.en: Yang Gongze, governor of Xiangzhou, had long served the house of Qujiang.
value.literal: Yang Gongze, governor of Xiangzhou, had been an old retainer of Qujiang.

value.zh: 每見幾，謂人曰：「康公此子，可謂桓靈寶出。」
value.en: Whenever he met Ji he would tell others, "Duke Kang's son is truly a Huan Lingbao come again."
value.literal: Whenever he saw Ji he would say to others, "Duke Kang's son may be called a Huan Lingbao reborn."

value.zh: 及公則卒，幾爲之誄，時年十五，沈約見而奇之，謂其舅蔡撙曰：「昨見賢甥楊平南誄文，不減希逸之作，始驗康公積善之慶。」
value.en: When Gongze died, Ji composed his funeral elegy at fifteen. Shen Yue read it with wonder and said to his uncle Cai Bo, "Yesterday I saw your worthy nephew's dirge for Yang, Pacifier of the South—not a step below Xiyi's writing; here is the first sign of Duke Kang's stored grace."
value.literal: When Gongze died, Ji wrote an elegy for him; he was fifteen. Shen Yue saw it and marveled, saying to his uncle Cai Bo, "Yesterday I read your worthy nephew's elegy for the Pacifier of the South, Yang—it is no whit inferior to Xiyi's work; this is the first proof of Duke Kang's accumulated good fortune."

value.zh: 釋褐著作佐郎、廬陵王文學、尚書殿中郎、太子舍人、掌管記，遷庶子、中書侍郎、尚書左丞。
value.en: After his first office he rose through Gentleman of the Palace Library, literary aide to the Prince of Luling, Secretariat gentleman in the palace bureau, crown prince attendant, and keeper of the records, then junior tutor, Secretariat gentleman, and left assistant in the Secretariat.
value.literal: On leaving the mourning garb he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library, literary aide to the Prince of Luling, Secretariat gentleman in the palace bureau, crown prince attendant, and keeper of the records; he was promoted to junior tutor, Secretariat gentleman, and left assistant in the Secretariat.

value.zh: 末年，專尚釋教。
value.en: In his last years he gave himself wholly to Buddhist teaching.
value.literal: In his later years he devoted himself solely to Buddhism.

value.zh: 爲新安太守，郡多山水，特其所好，適性遊履，遂爲之記。
value.en: Made magistrate of Xin'an, whose hills and streams were his special delight, he roamed at ease and composed a record of the commandery.
value.literal: As magistrate of Xin'an, a commandery rich in mountains and rivers that suited his temperament, he wandered as inclination led and wrote an account of the place.

value.zh: 卒於官。
value.en: He died while holding office.
value.literal: He died in office.

value.zh: 子爲，字元專，亦有文才。
value.en: His son Wei, styled Yuanzhuan, likewise showed a gift for letters.
value.literal: His son Wei, courtesy name Yuanzhuan, also had literary talent.

value.zh: 仕至太子舍人，永康令。
value.en: He served as crown prince attendant and magistrate of Yongkang.
value.literal: In office he reached crown prince attendant and magistrate of Yongkang.

value.zh: 趙倫之蕭思話臧燾
value.en: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, and Zang Dao
value.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao

value.zh: 介字茂鏡，少穎悟，有器識。
value.en: Jie, courtesy name Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.
value.literal: Jie, styled Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.

value.zh: 梁大同中，武陵王紀為揚州刺史，以介為府長史，在職以清白稱。
value.en: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.
value.literal: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.

value.zh: 武帝謂何敬容曰：「蕭介甚貧，可處以一郡。」
value.en: Emperor Wu told He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery."
value.literal: Emperor Wu said to He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery."

value.zh: 復曰：「始興郡頻無良守，可以介為之。」
value.en: He also said, "Shixing has often lacked good administrators — Jie may go there."
value.literal: He also said, "Shixing Commandery has often lacked good administrators — Jie may be sent there."

value.zh: 由是出為始興太守。
value.en: For this he went out as administrator of Shixing.
value.literal: For this he went out as Administrator of Shixing.

value.zh: 及至，甚著威德。
value.en: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.
value.literal: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.

value.zh: 列傳第二十九
value.en: the twenty-ninth year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies 29

value.zh: 第五弟孝勝，位尚書右丞、兼散騎常侍。
value.en: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.
value.literal: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.

value.zh: 聘魏還，為安西武陵王紀長史、蜀郡太守。
value.en: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.
value.literal: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.

value.zh: 紀僭號於蜀，以為尚書僕射。
value.en: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 隨紀出峽口，兵敗被執。
value.en: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.
value.literal: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.

value.zh: 元帝宥之，以為司徒右長史。
value.en: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 第七弟孝先，位武陵王主簿，與兄孝勝俱隨紀軍出峽口。
value.en: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian served as Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and, with his brother Xiaosheng, followed Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.
value.literal: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian was Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and followed his brother Xiaosheng with Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.

value.zh: 列傳第五十
value.en: the 50th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, number fifty.

value.zh: 時武陵王紀在東州，頗驕縱，上以臧盾性弱，不能匡正，召革慰遣，乃除武陵王長史、會稽郡丞，行府州事。
value.en: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature too weak to correct him, summoned Ge and dispatched him to the post of chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.
value.literal: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature weak and unable to correct him, summoned Ge to comfort and dispatch him, then appointed him chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.

value.zh: 革門生故吏家多在東，聞革應至，並賚持緣道迎候。
value.en: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east. Hearing that Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.
value.literal: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east; hearing Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.

value.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。」
value.en: Ge said, "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."
value.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."

value.zh: 至鎮唯資公俸，食不兼味。
value.en: Upon reaching his post he relied only on his official salary and ate no more than one dish at a meal.
value.literal: Upon reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.

value.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辯析，曾無疑滯，人安吏畏，百城震恐。
value.en: The commandery's territory was broad and populous, with hundreds of lawsuits each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without hesitation. The people were at peace, the clerks feared him, and the hundred cities trembled in awe.
value.literal: The commandery's territory was broad and populous; lawsuits numbered hundreds each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without ever hesitating. The people were at peace and the clerks feared him; the hundred cities trembled in awe.

value.zh: 琅邪王騫為山陰令，贓貨狼籍，望風自解。
value.en: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere. At the news of Ge's arrival he resigned of his own accord.
value.literal: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere; at the news he resigned of his own accord.

value.zh: 府王憚之。
value.en: The prince of the domain feared him.
value.literal: The prince of the domain feared him.

value.zh: 每侍燕，言論必以詩、書，王因此耽學好文。
value.en: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents. Because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.
value.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents; because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.

value.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈武帝，帝謂僕射徐勉曰：「革果稱職。」
value.en: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."
value.literal: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Ge truly fills his post."

value.zh: 乃除都官尚書。
value.en: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.
value.literal: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.

value.zh: 將還，贈遺一無所受，送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，唯乘台所給一舸。
value.en: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.
value.literal: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.

value.zh: 舸艚偏欹，不得安臥。
value.en: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.
value.literal: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.

value.zh: 或請濟江徙重物以迮輕艚，革既無物，乃於西陵岸取石十餘片以實之。
value.en: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.
value.literal: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.

value.zh: 其清貧如此。
value.en: Such was his purity and poverty.
value.literal: Such was his purity and poverty.

value.zh: 武陵王出鎮江州，乃曰：「我得江革文，得革清貧，豈能一日忘之，當與其同飽。」
value.en: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said, "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share my table with him."
value.literal: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said: "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share fullness with him."

value.zh: 乃表革同行。
value.en: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.
value.literal: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.

value.zh: 除南中郎長史、尋陽太守。
value.en: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.
value.literal: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.

value.zh: 征入為度支尚書。
value.en: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.
value.literal: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.

value.zh: 好獎進閭閻，為後生延譽，由是衣冠士子翕然歸之。
value.en: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations. Thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.
value.literal: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations; thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.

value.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。
value.en: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed were not the right men.
value.literal: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed in order were not the right men.

value.zh: 革性強直，每朝宴恒有褒貶，以此為權貴所疾。
value.en: Ge's nature was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he always had praise and blame to offer, and for this the powerful and noble resented him.
value.literal: Ge's nature was forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame, and for this was resented by the powerful and noble.

value.zh: 乃謝病還家，除光祿大夫，優遊閑放，以文酒自娛。
value.en: He then pleaded illness and returned home. Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, he lived at leisure and found pleasure in literature and wine.
value.literal: He then pleaded illness and returned home, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and lived at leisure in ease, finding pleasure in literature and wine.

value.zh: 卒，諡曰強子。
value.en: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Qiangzi.
value.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Qiangzi.

value.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。
value.en: His collected works of twenty scrolls circulated widely.
value.literal: He had a collection of writings of twenty scrolls circulating in the world.

value.zh: 革曆官八府長史，四王行事，三為二千石，傍無姬侍，家徒壁立，時以此高之。
value.en: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, and three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official. He had no concubines at his side and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.
value.literal: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official, had no concubines at his side, and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.

value.zh: 長子行敏早卒，次子德藻。
value.en: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.
value.literal: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.

value.zh: 列傳第五十三
value.en: the 53th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three

value.zh: 先是，天監中沙門釋寶志為讖云：「太歲龍，將無理。
value.en: Earlier, during the Tianjian reign, the monk Baozhi uttered a prophecy: "When the Tai Sui year is the Dragon, the leader will lose legitimacy.
value.literal: Earlier, in the Tianjian era, the monk Shi Baozhi made a prophecy saying: "In the year of the Dragon of Tai Sui, the general will be without reason.

value.zh: 蕭經霜，草應死。
value.en: The House of Xiao passes through frost; the grass must wither.
value.literal: The Xiao clan meets frost; the grass should die.

value.zh: 餘人散，十八子。」
value.en: The commoners disperse; 'ten,' 'eight,' and 'son.'"
value.literal: The rest of the people scatter; eighteen sons."

value.zh: 時言蕭氏當滅，李氏代興。
value.en: People read the verses as foretelling the fall of the Xiao and the rise of the Li.
value.literal: At the time it was said the Xiao clan would perish and the Li clan would rise in its place.

value.zh: 及湘州賊陸納等攻破衡州刺史丁道貴，而李洪雅又自零陵稱助討納。
value.en: When the rebel Lu Na of Xiangzhou overran Hengzhou and its inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya proclaimed from Lingling that he had come to help crush Na.
value.literal: When the Xiangzhou rebels Lu Na and others attacked and broke Hengzhou Inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya moreover from Lingling declared himself aiding in punishing Na.

value.zh: 既而朝廷未達其心，詔征僧辯就宜豐侯循南征，為都督東上諸軍事。
value.en: The court still misread his intentions and ordered Senbian to march south with the Marquis of Yifeng, appointing him commander of all eastern armies.
value.literal: Soon the court did not fathom his heart; an edict summoned Senbian to join Marquis Xun of Yifeng in a southern campaign, making him Commander-in-Chief of all eastern forces.

value.zh: 以陳武帝為都督西下諸軍事。
value.en: Chen Wudi was placed in command of all western forces.
value.literal: Chen Wudi was made Commander-in-Chief of all western-downward military affairs.

value.zh: 先是，陳武讓都督于僧辯，僧辯不受，故元帝分為東西都督而俱南討焉。
value.en: Earlier Chen Wu had offered Senbian supreme command, which Senbian refused; Emperor Yuan therefore split command into eastern and western wings and sent both south.
value.literal: Earlier, Chen Wu had yielded the commandership to Senbian, but Senbian did not accept; therefore Emperor Yuan divided east and west commanderships and both marched south to punish.

value.zh: 尋而洪雅降納，納以為應符，於是共議拜洪雅為大將軍，尊事為主。
value.en: Hongya soon joined Na, who took this as confirmation of the prophecy; the rebels then agreed to make Hongya their generalissimo and acknowledged him as their sovereign.
value.literal: Soon Hongya surrendered to Na; Na took it as fulfillment of the prophecy, and they jointly deliberated to invest Hongya as Grand General and honor him as lord.

value.zh: 洪雅乘平肩大輿，傘蓋、鼓吹，羽儀悉備，翼從入長沙城。
value.en: Hongya entered Changsha in a state carriage with parasols, musical escort, and full ceremonial guard.
value.literal: Hongya rode a level-shoulder great carriage; parasols, canopies, drums and pipes—all regalia fully prepared—he entered Changsha city with wings of attendants.

value.zh: 時納等據車輪，夾岸為城，士卒皆百戰之餘，器甲精嚴，徒黨勇銳，蒙沖鬥艦，亙水陵山。
value.en: Na held Chelun, fortifying both banks; his troops were hardened veterans with superb arms, his followers fierce, and his covered ships lined the waterway from shore to hill.
value.literal: At the time Na and others held Chelun, building walls on both banks; the soldiers were all veterans of a hundred battles, weapons and armor exquisitely strict, followers brave and sharp, covered raiders and fighting ships spanning water and overrunning hills.

value.zh: 時天日清明，初無雲霧，軍發之際，忽然風雨，時人謂為泣軍，百姓竊言知其敗也。
value.en: The sky had been clear, yet the moment the army marched a storm broke; people called it the army weeping, and locals whispered that defeat was foretold.
value.literal: At the time heaven's sun was clear and bright, at first without cloud or mist; at the moment the army set out, suddenly wind and rain—people of the time called it a weeping army, and common people whispered that they knew defeat was coming.

value.zh: 三月庚寅，有兩龍自城西江中騰躍升天，五色分明，遙映江水。
value.en: On the third month's gengyin day, two dragons rose from the river west of the city into the sky, their five colors vivid against the distant water.
value.literal: On the gengyin day of the third month, two dragons leapt from the river west of the city soaring up to heaven, five colors distinct, reflecting distantly in the river water.

value.zh: 百姓咸仰面目之，父老或聚而悲，竊相謂曰：「地龍已去，國其亡乎。」
value.en: People gazed up at them; some elders wept together and murmured: "The earth dragons have gone—surely the realm is doomed."
value.literal: The common people all looked up at their faces; elders sometimes gathered and wept, whispering to one another: "The earth dragons have departed—will the state perish?"

value.zh: 初，納造大艦，一名曰三王艦者，邵陵王、河東王、桂陽嗣王三人並為元帝所害，故立其像於艦，祭乙太牢，加其節蓋羽儀鼓吹，每戰輒祭之以求福。
value.en: Na had built a great warship, the Three Kings Ship, for the three princes Shaoling, Hedong, and Guiyang whom Emperor Yuan had killed; he set up their images aboard, sacrificed oxen to them with full honors, and before every battle offered prayers for luck.
value.literal: Earlier, Na built a great ship called the Three Kings Ship—for the Prince of Shaoling, Prince of Hedong, and Prince of Guiyang, three men all killed by Emperor Yuan—therefore he erected their images on the ship, offering yi and ta lao sacrifices, adding their banners, canopies, regalia, drums and pipes; before each battle he would sacrifice to them seeking fortune.

value.zh: 又造二艦，一曰青龍艦，一曰白虎艦，皆衣以牛皮，並高十五丈，選其中尤勇健者乘之。
value.en: He also built two tower ships, the Azure Dragon and the White Tiger, sheathed in ox hide and fifteen zhang tall, crewed by his fiercest warriors.
value.literal: He also built two ships—one called the Azure Dragon Ship, one called the White Tiger Ship—both clad in ox hide, each fifteen zhang high, selecting from among them the most courageous and strong to man them.

value.zh: 僧辯憚之，稍作連城以逼焉。
value.en: Senbian, wary of these vessels, began building linked fortifications to press in on them.
value.literal: Senbian feared them, and slightly built linked ramparts to press upon them.

value.zh: 賊不敢交鋒，並懷懈怠。
value.en: The rebels would not engage and grew complacent.
value.literal: The rebels did not dare cross blades, and all harbored slackness.

value.zh: 僧辯因其無備，親執旗鼓以誡進止，群賊大敗，歸保長沙。
value.en: Senbian seized their negligence, personally directing the drums and banners; the rebels were routed and fled back to Changsha.
value.literal: Senbian, because they were unprepared, personally took drum and banner to admonish advance and halt; the rebel host was greatly defeated and returned to defend Changsha.

value.zh: 僧辯乃命築壘圍之，而自出臨視。
value.en: Senbian ordered siege works built and went out personally to supervise them.
value.literal: Senbian then ordered building ramparts to besiege them, and himself went out to oversee in person.

value.zh: 賊知不設備，其党吳藏、李賢明等蒙楯直進，僧辯尚據胡床不為之動，指麾勇敢，遂斬賢明，賊乃退歸。
value.en: The rebels thought him undefended; Wu Zang, Li Xianming, and others charged under shield cover. Senbian did not rise from his camp chair, coolly directing the fight until Xianming was slain and the attackers fell back.
value.literal: The rebels, knowing he was unguarded, his partisans Wu Zang, Li Xianming and others covered with shields advanced straight on; Senbian still sat on a folding camp chair unmoved, directing with bravery, and thereupon cut down Xianming—the rebels then withdrew.

value.zh: 初，陵納作逆，以王琳為辭，云：「若放琳則自服」。
value.en: When Lu Na first rebelled, he declared: "If Wang Lin were freed, I would submit."
value.literal: Earlier, when Lu Na rebelled, he used Wang Lin as his pretext, saying: "If Lin is released, I will submit myself."

value.zh: 時眾軍未之許，而武陵王紀擁眾上流，內外駭懼。
value.en: The allied armies refused, even as Prince Ji of Wuling massed forces upriver; court and camp alike were terrified.
value.literal: At the time the various armies did not agree to it, while Prince Ji of Wuling gathered troops upstream; inside and outside were alarmed and fearful.

value.zh: 元帝乃遣琳和解之，湘州乃平。
value.en: Emperor Yuan dispatched Wang Lin to negotiate; Xiangzhou was finally pacified.
value.literal: Emperor Yuan then sent Lin to mediate and reconcile; Xiangzhou was then pacified.

value.zh: 因被詔會眾軍西討。
value.en: He was then ordered to gather the armies for the western campaign.
value.literal: Thereupon he received an edict to assemble the armies for a western punitive campaign.

value.zh: 尋而武陵敗績。
value.en: Prince Ji of Wuling was soon crushed.
value.literal: Soon Wuling suffered defeat.

value.zh: 列傳第五十九
value.en: the 59th year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine

value.zh: 時有蕭濟字孝康，東海蘭陵人也。
value.en: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, from Lanling in Donghai commandery.
value.literal: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, a native of Lanling in Donghai.

value.zh: 好學，博通經史。
value.en: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
value.literal: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

value.zh: 仕梁為太子舍人。
value.en: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 預平侯景功，封松陽縣侯。
value.en: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.
value.literal: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.

value.zh: 陳文帝為會稽太守，以濟為宣毅府長史。
value.en: When Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment.
value.literal: When Chen Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji Chief Secretary of the Firm Resolution Establishment.

value.zh: 及即位，授侍中。
value.en: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 太建中，歷位五兵、度支、祠部三尚書，卒。
value.en: During the Taijian era he successively served as Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.
value.literal: During the Taijian era he successively held the three posts of Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.

value.zh: 三十一年春正月甲戌朔，以日食，不受朝。
value.en: Year 31, spring, jiaxu new moon: Gaozong canceled audience for the eclipse.
value.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, day jiaxu new moon: because of a solar eclipse, court audience was not held.

value.zh: 丁丑，雷。
value.en: On dingchou, thunder rolled.
value.literal: Day dingchou: thunder.

value.zh: 丁亥，免湖州增丁所輸絹。
value.en: On dinghai, Huzhou was freed from added-household silk levies.
value.literal: Day dinghai: the silk paid by Huzhou for added registered households was remitted.

value.zh: 夜，風雷雨雪交作。
value.en: That night wind, thunder, snow, and rain came together.
value.literal: At night, wind, thunder, snow, and rain struck together.

value.zh: 辛卯，詔江、浙官民戶均輸和市絁帛。
value.en: On xinmao, Jiang and Zhe were told to share silk transport and market purchases equally among official and common households.
value.literal: Day xinmao: an edict ordered official and common households of Jiang and Zhe to share equally in transport and market purchase of silk.

value.zh: 壬辰，劉寶落節鉞、福建路居住。
value.en: On renchen, Liu Bao lost his command tally and was sent to live on the Fujian circuit.
value.literal: Day renchen: Liu Bao was stripped of his command tally and made to reside on the Fujian circuit.

value.zh: 丙申，大雨雪，給三衙衛士、行在貧民錢及薪炭，命常平振給輔郡細民，諸路監司決獄。
value.en: On bingchen, heavy snow brought cash and charcoal to palace guards and capital poor; Ever-Normal stores fed nearby counties; commissioners judged cases.
value.literal: Day bingchen: in great rain and snow, money and fuel were given to the Three Yamaz guards and poor people at the mobile court; the Ever-Normal Granaries were ordered to relieve needy folk in auxiliary commanderies; circuit commissioners were to decide cases.

value.zh: 己亥，放張浚、胡銓自便。
value.en: On jihai, Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were freed to their own devices.
value.literal: Day jihai: Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were released to go as they pleased.

value.zh: 庚子，禁淮南拘籍戶馬。
value.en: On gengzi, Huainan could no longer seize and register civilian horses.
value.literal: Day gengzi: Huainan was forbidden to seize and register household horses.

value.zh: 九月庚午朔，命大臣朝饗太廟。
value.en: Ninth month, gengwu new moon: great ministers offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
value.literal: Ninth month, day gengwu new moon: great ministers were ordered to offer at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

value.zh: 辛未，宗祀徽宗於明堂，以配上帝，大赦。
value.en: On xinwei, Huizong was enshrined in the Bright Hall with the High God; a great amnesty followed.
value.literal: Day xinwei: Emperor Huizong was enshrined in the Bright Hall with the High God as correlate; a great amnesty was proclaimed.

value.zh: 甲戌，金人犯黃牛堡，守將李彥堅拒卻之，金兵遂扼大散關，吳璘駐青野原，遣將高松等援之。
value.en: On jiaxu, Jin hit Huangniu Fort and Li Yanjian drove them off; they seized Dasan Pass; Wu Lin camped Qingye Plain and sent Gao Song to help.
value.literal: Day jiaxu: Jin troops attacked Huangniu Fort; defender Li Yanjian repulsed them; the Jin then blocked Dasan Pass; Wu Lin camped at Qingye Plain and sent Generals Gao Song and others to reinforce.

value.zh: 庚辰，以給事中黃祖舜同知樞密院事。
value.en: On gengchen, Huang Zushun became Associate Privy Council Signatory.
value.literal: Day gengchen: Supervising Secretary Huang Zushun was made Associate Privy Council Signatory.

value.zh: 壬午，流星晝隕。
value.en: On renwu, a meteor fell by day.
value.literal: Day renwu: a meteor fell in daylight.

value.zh: 乙酉，詔劉錡、王權、李顯忠、戚方嚴備清河、潁河、渦河口。
value.en: On yiyou, Liu Qi, Wang Quan, Li Xianzhong, and Qi Fang were told to brace Qinghe, Yinghe, and Guo mouths.
value.literal: Day yiyou: an edict ordered Liu Qi, Wang Quan, Li Xianzhong, and Qi Fang to ready Qinghe, Yinghe, and Guohe mouths strictly.

value.zh: 丁亥，成閔渡江，屯應城縣，遣吳拱戍郢州。
value.en: On dinghai, Cheng Min crossed to Yingcheng and posted Wu Gong at Yingzhou.
value.literal: Day dinghai: Cheng Min crossed the river and camped at Yingcheng county; he sent Wu Gong to garrison Yingzhou.

value.zh: 博州民王友直聚兵大名，自稱河北安撫制置使，以其徒王任為副，遣軍師馮穀入朝奏事。
value.en: Wang Youzhi of Bozhou raised Daming, called himself Hebei pacification commissioner, made Wang Ren vice, and sent Feng Gu to court.
value.literal: Bozhou commoner Wang Youzhi gathered troops at Daming, styled himself Hebei pacification commissioner, made his follower Wang Ren vice, and sent strategist Feng Gu to court to report.

value.zh: 吳璘遣將彭青至寶雞渭河，夜劫金人橋頭砦，破之。
value.en: Wu Lin's Peng Qing reached the Baoji Wei, raided the bridgehead fort by night, and took it.
value.literal: Wu Lin sent General Peng Qing to the Baoji Wei River; at night he raided the Jin bridgehead fort and broke it.

value.zh: 庚寅，成閔遣統制趙撙部兵五千駐德安。
value.en: On gengyin, Cheng Min sent Zhao Zan with five thousand to De'an.
value.literal: Day gengyin: Cheng Min sent controller Zhao Zan with five thousand to camp at De'an.

value.zh: 辛卯，金國趣使臣書至楚州，守臣以聞，其辭多悖慢。
value.en: On xinmao, an insolent Jin dispatch reached Chuzhou and the prefect reported it.
value.literal: Day xinmao: a Jin urgent dispatch reached Chuzhou; the prefect reported it—its wording was mostly insolent.

value.zh: 壬辰，監盱眙軍淮河渡夏俊復泗州。
value.en: On renchen, Xia Jun of the Chuyang garrison retook Sizhou.
value.literal: Day renchen: Chuyang garrison inspector Xia Jun recovered Sizhou.

value.zh: 癸巳，金人犯通化軍，守將張超拒卻之。
value.en: On guisi, Jin hit Tonghua Army and Zhang Chao drove them back.
value.literal: Day guisi: Jin troops attacked Tonghua Army; defender Zhang Chao repulsed them.

value.zh: 甲午，冊諡大行皇帝曰恭文順德仁孝皇帝，廟號欽宗。
value.en: On jiawu, the late emperor was styled Respectful, Cultured, Accordant, Virtuous, and Filial with temple name Qinzong.
value.literal: Day jiawu: the late emperor was given the temple posthumous title Respectful, Cultured, Accordant, Virtuous, and Filial and the temple name Qinzong.

value.zh: 吳璘遣將劉海復秦州，金守將蕭濟降。
value.en: Wu Lin's Liu Hai retook Qinzhou; the Jin prefect Xiao Ji surrendered.
value.literal: Wu Lin sent General Liu Hai to recover Qinzhou; Jin prefect Xiao Ji submitted.

value.zh: 乙未，金人犯信陽軍。
value.en: On yiwei, Jin attacked Xinyang Army.
value.literal: Day yiwei: Jin troops attacked Xinyang Army.

value.zh: 丙申，吳璘遣將曹㳜復洮州。
value.en: On bingshen, Wu Lin's Cao Sui retook Taozhou.
value.literal: Day bingshen: Wu Lin sent General Cao Sui to recover Taozhou.

value.zh: 戊戌，劉錡發揚州。
value.en: On wuxu, Liu Qi marched from Yangzhou.
value.literal: Day wuxu: Liu Qi marched from Yangzhou.

value.zh: 詔以金人背盟，降敕榜招諭中原軍民。
value.en: Because the Jin had broken treaty, a placard called the central plain to arms.
value.literal: An edict, because the Jin had broken the alliance, issued a placard to summon the armies and people of the central plain.

value.zh: 己亥，蘭州漢軍千戶王宏殺其刺史溫敦烏乜來降。
value.en: On jihai, Lanzhou Han officer Wang Hong killed Commissioner Wendun Wuma and defected.
value.literal: Day jihai: Wang Hong, a thousand-household chief of the Lanzhou Han army, killed his commissioner Wendun Wuma and came over.

value.zh: 吳璘遣將彭青復隴州。
value.en: Wu Lin's Peng Qing retook Longzhou.
value.literal: Wu Lin sent General Peng Qing to recover Longzhou.

value.zh: 是月，金主亮以尚書右丞李通為大都督，造浮梁于淮水之上，遂自將來攻，兵號百萬，遠近大震。
value.en: That month Hailing made Li Tong grand marshal, bridged the Huai, and came himself with a host said at a million; the realm shook.
value.literal: That month, the Jin ruler Hailing made Right Vice Director Li Tong grand marshal, built pontoon bridges on the Huai, then came in person to attack; his troops were said to number a million; near and far were greatly shaken.

value.zh: 自夫有天地焉，有人物焉，樹司牧以君臨，懸政教而成務，莫不擬乾坤之大象，稟中和以建極，揆影響之幽賾，成律呂之精微。
value.en: From the moment Heaven and Earth existed and humanity arose, every ruler who governed and every state that taught its people modeled itself on the cosmos, drew on cosmic balance to set standards, read nature's hidden signs, and perfected the science of pitch and measure.
value.literal: Since there have been Heaven and Earth, and since there have been people and things, in establishing rulers to govern and in setting forth government and teaching to accomplish their tasks, none have failed to take the great images of Heaven and Earth as their model, to receive the Mean and Harmony in establishing the supreme standard, to measure the hidden depths of shadow and influence, and to achieve the subtle refinements of pitch pipes and bell tones.

value.zh: 是用範圍百度，財成萬品。
value.en: Thus they regulated all standards and shaped the ten thousand kinds of things.
value.literal: By this means they encompassed the hundred measures and completed the myriad things.

value.zh: 昔者淳古葦籥，創睹人籟之源，女媧笙簧，仍昭鳳律之首。
value.en: In deepest antiquity, reed flutes first disclosed the origin of human music; Nüwa's reed pipes still marked the first phoenix-toned pitch.
value.literal: In antiquity, in the pure ancient age, reed pipes first revealed the source of human sounds; Nüwa's sheng and huang still proclaimed the beginning of the phoenix pitch.

value.zh: 後聖廣業，稽古彌崇，伶倫含少，乃擅比竹之工，虞舜昭華，方傳刻玉之美。
value.en: Later sages enlarged the tradition and revered the past: Ling Lun's "Containing the Lesser" perfected the art of calibrated bamboo pipes; Yu Shun's Bright Splendor preserved the craft of jade pitch pipes.
value.literal: Later sages expanded the enterprise and honored antiquity ever more highly: Ling Lun's Han Shao mastered the craft of comparing bamboo tubes; Shun of Yu with Zhao Hua transmitted the beauty of carving jade.

value.zh: 是以《書》稱：「葉時月正日，同律度量衡。」
value.en: Hence the Documents states: "Align the seasons, months, and corrected day with unified pitch pipes, measures, and weights."
value.literal: Therefore the Book of Documents says: "The seasons, the months, the corrected day, and the pitch pipes, measures, and weights are all in accord.

value.zh: 又曰：「予欲聞六律、五聲、八音、七始詠，以出納五言。」
value.en: It also says: "I desire to hear the six pitch standards, five tones, eight timbres, and seven beginnings sung, to produce and receive the five-word verses."
value.literal: It also says: "I wish to hear the six pitch standards, the five notes, the eight timbres, and the seven beginnings chanted, so as to bring forth and receive the five words."

value.zh: 此皆候金常而列管，憑璿璣以運鈞，統三極之元，紀七衡之響，可以作樂崇德，殷薦上帝。
value.en: These all depend on metal bells to set the pipes, on the armillary instrument to drive the steelyard, to unify the three cosmic poles and mark the seven celestial harmonies—making music to ennoble virtue and richly offering worship to Heaven.
value.literal: All these await the constant of metal to array the pipes, rely on the armillary sphere to turn the steelyard, unify the origin of the three ultimates, and record the resonance of the seven armillary rings—they can be used to make music and exalt virtue, and abundantly to offer to the Supreme Lord.

value.zh: 故能動天地，感鬼神，和人心，移風俗，考得失，徵成敗者也。
value.en: Music thus moves Heaven and Earth, stirs spirits, harmonizes hearts, changes customs, and reveals success or failure.
value.literal: Therefore they can move Heaven and Earth, touch spirits and ghosts, harmonize human hearts, transform customs, examine gain and loss, and verify success and failure.

value.zh: 粵在夏、商，無聞改作。
value.en: Under Xia and Shang, no alterations to the system are recorded.
value.literal: In Xia and Shang, nothing is recorded of changes or new creations.

value.zh: 其于《周禮》，曲同則「掌六律六同之和，以辨天地四方陰陽之聲，以為樂器。」
value.en: The Rites of Zhou's section on pitch concordance says: "He oversees the harmony of the six pitch standards and six concordances, distinguishing the sounds of Heaven, Earth, the four directions, and yin and yang, for use in instruments."
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, in the section on pitch concordance, it states: "He manages the harmony of the six pitch standards and six concordances, to distinguish the sounds of Heaven and Earth, the four directions, yin and yang, and to make them into musical instruments.

value.zh: 景王鑄鐘，問律於泠州鳩，對曰：「夫律者，所以立鈞出度。」
value.en: When King Jing of Zhou cast bells, he asked Leng Zhoujiu about pitch; the reply was: "Pitch standards establish the steelyard and derive all measures."
value.literal: When King Jing cast bells, he inquired about pitch from Leng Zhoujiu, who replied: "Pitch standards are what establish the steelyard and produce measures."

value.zh: 鈞有五，則權衡規矩準繩鹹備。
value.en: With five parts to the steelyard, scales, weights, compasses, squares, plumb lines, and measuring cords all follow.
value.literal: When the steelyard has five parts, then scales, steelyard-weights, compasses, squares, plumb lines, and measuring cords are all complete.

value.zh: 故《詩》曰：「尹氏太師，執國之鈞，天子是裨，俾眾不迷」是也。
value.en: As the Odes put it: "Grand Master Yin holds the nation's steelyard, assists the Son of Heaven, and keeps the people from losing their way."
value.literal: Thus the Odes say: "The Grand Master Yin, holding the state's steelyard, assists the Son of Heaven and keeps the multitude from going astray"—this is the meaning.

value.zh: 太史公《律書》云：「王者制事立物，法度軌則，一稟於六律，為萬事之本。
value.en: Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards states: "The king, in ordering affairs and setting standards, derives all laws and measures from the six pitch standards—the foundation of everything.
value.literal: Grand Historian Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards says: "The king, in establishing affairs and setting things in order, with laws, measures, and rules, takes the six pitch standards as the single source—the root of the ten thousand affairs.

value.zh: 其于兵械，尤所重焉。
value.en: They are held in particular esteem for military equipment.
value.literal: In military weapons, they are especially valued.

value.zh: 故云：「望敵知吉凶，聞聲效勝負。
value.en: Hence the saying: "Look at the enemy and know fortune or misfortune; listen to sounds and foretell victory or defeat.
value.literal: Therefore it is said: "Gazing at the enemy reveals good or ill fortune; hearing sounds predicts victory or defeat."

value.zh: 百王不易之道也。」
value.en: This is the unchanging principle of all dynasties."
value.literal: This is the Way that the hundred kings have never changed.

value.en: End of quotation.
value.literal: Close quotation mark.

value.zh: 徐廣、徐爰、王隱等《晉書》云：「武帝泰始九年，中書監荀勖校太樂八音，不和，始知為後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。
value.en: The Jin History of Xu Guang, Xu Yuan, Wang Yin, and others records: "In the ninth year of Taishi, Xun Xu, Supervisor of the Secretariat, checked the eight timbres of the Grand Music and found them discordant; only then did he understand that from Later Han to Wei the chi had grown more than four fen longer than the ancient measure.
value.literal: Xu Guang, Xu Ai, Wang Yin, and others' Jin History says: "In Emperor Wu's Taishi ninth year, Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu corrected the Grand Music eight timbres—they were not harmonious; then knowing that from Later Han through Wei the foot measure was more than four fen longer than antiquity.

value.zh: 勖乃部著作郎劉恭，依《周禮》制尺，所謂古尺也。
value.en: Xu ordered Liu Gong to make a Rites of Zhou foot measure—the ancient standard.
value.literal: Xu then ordered Editorial Director Liu Gong to make a foot measure according to the Rites of Zhou—the so-called ancient foot measure.

value.zh: 依古尺更鑄銅律呂，以調聲韻。
value.en: Using the ancient measure, bronze pitch pipes were recast to restore harmony.
value.literal: According to the ancient foot measure, bronze pitch pipes and bell tones were recast to tune sound and pitch.

value.zh: 以尺量古器，與本銘尺寸無差。
value.en: Ancient vessels measured against it matched their inscriptions exactly.
value.literal: Using the foot measure to measure ancient vessels, there was no discrepancy with original inscription dimensions.

value.zh: 又汲郡盜發魏襄王塚，得古周時玉律及鐘磬，與新律聲韻暗同。
value.en: Ji commandery tomb robbers found Zhou jade pitch pipes and bells matching the new standards.
value.literal: Also the Ji commandery tomb robbers opened King Xiang of Wei's tomb, obtaining ancient Zhou jade pitch standards and bells and chime stones—their sound and pitch darkly matched the new pitch standards.

value.zh: 于時郡國或得漢時故鐘，吹新律命之，皆應。」
value.en: Han-era bells found in the provinces all matched when tested against the new pipes."
value.literal: At the time in commanderies and kingdoms, Han-era old bells were sometimes obtained; blowing the new pitch standards to tune them—all responded.

value.zh: 梁武《鐘律緯》云：「祖沖之所傳銅尺，其銘曰：'晉泰始十年，中書考古器，揆校今尺，長四分半。
value.en: Liang Wu's Treatise cites Zu Chongzhi's copper measure: "tenth year of Jin of Taishi—four fen and a half longer than the present measure.
value.literal: Liang Wu's Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes says: "The copper foot measure transmitted by Zu Chongzhi—its inscription says: 'Jin Taishi tenth year, the Secretariat examined ancient vessels and compared the present foot measure—it is four fen and a half longer.

value.zh: 所校古法有七品：一曰姑洗玉律，二曰小呂玉律，三曰西京銅望臬，四曰金錯望臬，五曰銅斛，六曰古錢，七曰建武銅尺。
value.en: Seven ancient reference standards were tested: Maiden Wash jade pipe, Lesser Bell jade pipe, Western Capital bronze gnomon, gold-inlaid gnomon, copper hu, ancient coins, and Jianwu copper measure.
value.literal: The ancient methods examined had seven grades: first, Maiden Wash jade pitch standard; second, Lesser Bell jade pitch standard; third, Western Capital bronze gnomon table; fourth, gold-inlaid gnomon table; fifth, copper hu; sixth, ancient coins; seventh, Jianwu copper foot measure.

value.zh: 姑洗微強，西京望臬微弱，其餘與此尺同。
value.en: Maiden Wash ran slightly high; the Western Capital gnomon slightly low—the rest matched.
value.literal: Maiden Wash was slightly strong; Western Capital gnomon table slightly weak—the rest matched this foot measure.

value.zh: '銘八十二字。
value.en: The inscription contains eighty-two characters.
value.literal: Inscription: eighty-two characters.

value.zh: 此尺者，勖新尺也。
value.en: This is Xu's new measure.
value.literal: This foot measure is Xu's new foot measure.

value.zh: 今尺者，杜夔尺也。
value.en: The contemporary measure is Du Kui's.
value.literal: Today's foot measure is Du Kui's foot measure.

value.zh: 雷次宗、何胤之二人作《鐘律圖》，所載荀勖校量古尺文，與此銘同。
value.en: Lei Cizong and He Yin's Diagram records the same Xun Xu examination text.
value.literal: Lei Cizong and He Yin's two authors' Diagram of Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes records Xun Xu's examination text of the ancient foot measure—the same as this inscription.

value.zh: 而蕭吉樂譜，謂為梁朝所考七品，謬也。
value.en: Xiao Ji wrongly attributes these to Liang-era examination.
