value.literal: But Xiao Ji's Music Treatise calls it the seven grades examined by the Liang court—this is erroneous.

value.zh: 今以此尺為本，以校諸代尺」雲。
value.en: This measure serves as the base for comparing all dynastic foot measures."
value.literal: Now taking this foot measure as base to compare foot measures of various dynasties."

value.zh: 蕭吉云：「出於《司馬法》。
value.en: Xiao Ji says, "It comes from the Sima Methods.
value.literal: Xiao Ji says: "It comes from the Sima Methods.

value.zh: 梁朝刻其度於影表，以測影。」
value.en: The Liang court carved its measure on a gnomon table for shadow measurement."
value.literal: The Liang court carved its measure on the shadow table to measure shadows.

value.zh: 案此即奉朝請祖暅所算造銅主影表者也。
value.en: This is Court Gentleman Zu Geng's calculated bronze gnomon table.
value.literal: Examining this—it is the bronze gnomon shadow table calculated and made by Court Gentleman Zu Geng.

value.zh: 經陳滅入朝。
value.en: It entered the court after Chen's fall.
value.literal: After Chen's fall it entered the court.

value.zh: 大業中，議以合古，乃用之調律，以制鐘磬等八音樂器。
value.en: In Daye, it was deemed most antiquity-conforming and used to tune bells, chimes, and the eight timbres.
value.literal: In the Daye era, discussion held it accorded with antiquity; therefore it was used to tune pitch standards and make bells, chime stones, and the eight timbres.

value.zh: 蕭吉《樂譜》云：「漢章帝時，零陵文學史奚景於泠道縣舜廟下得玉律，度為此尺。」
value.en: Xiao Ji records: "In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, the scholar Xi Jing of Lingling found a jade pitch pipe beneath Shun's temple in Lengdao county and derived this measure."
value.literal: Xiao Ji's Music Treatise says: "In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, Lingling Literary Scholar Xi Jing at Shun's temple in Lengdao county obtained a jade pitch standard and made this foot measure from it.

value.zh: 傅暢《晉諸公贊》云：「葛勖造鐘律，時人並稱其精密，唯陳留阮鹹，譏其聲高。
value.en: Fu Chang records: "Ge Xun's standards were praised by contemporaries for precision; only Ruan Xian of Chenliu criticized the pitch as too high.
value.literal: Fu Chang's Jin Worthies' Praise says: "Ge Xun made bell and pitch standards; people all praised their precision—only Chenliu Ruan Xian criticized their sound as high.

value.zh: 後始平掘地，得古銅尺，歲久欲腐，以校荀勖今尺，短校四分。
value.en: Later at Shiping, a decayed ancient copper measure proved four fen shorter than Xun Xu's—vindicating Ruan Xian.
value.literal: Later at Shiping, excavating the ground, an ancient copper foot measure was obtained—long decayed; comparing with Xun Xu's present foot measure, it was four fen shorter in comparison.

value.zh: 時人以咸為解。」
value.en: Contemporaries acknowledged Ruan Xian was correct."
value.literal: People of the time took Xian as having understood."

value.zh: 此兩尺長短近同。
value.en: These two measures are nearly identical.
value.literal: These two foot measures' lengths are nearly the same.

value.zh: 蕭吉雲，晉氏江東所用。
value.en: Xiao Ji says Eastern Jin used this measure in Jiangdong.
value.literal: Xiao Ji says the Jin clan used this in Jiangdong.

value.zh: 序《洪範五行傳》曰：「視之不明，是謂不知。
value.en: The preface to the Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When sight is dim, it is called ignorance.
value.literal: The preface to the Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When vision is not clear, this is called not knowing.

value.zh: 厥咎舒，厥罰常燠，厥極疾。
value.en: The fault is slackness; the penalty is unrelenting heat; the ultimate consequence is disease.
value.literal: Its fault is laxity; its punishment is constant heat; its extreme is illness.

value.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有羽蟲之孽。
value.en: In such seasons grass-spirits appear, and calamities wrought by winged creatures arise.
value.literal: At such times there are grass demons; at such times there are calamities of winged insects.

value.zh: 故有羊禍，故有目疾，有赤眚赤祥。
value.en: Hence come sheep omens, eye afflictions, and baleful red signs.
value.literal: Therefore there are sheep portents; therefore there are eye ailments, red disasters and red omens.

value.zh: 惟水沴火。」
value.en: Water alone overcomes fire."
value.literal: Only water harms fire.'"

value.zh: 常燠後齊天保八年三月，大熱，人或暍死。
value.en: As for "constant heat": in the third month of Northern Qi's Tianbao year 8, the heat was extreme, and people died of sunstroke.
value.literal: Constant heat'—afterward, in the third month of the eighth year of Tianbao of Northern Qi, there was great heat, and some people died of heatstroke.

value.zh: 劉向《五行傳》曰：「視不明，用近習，賢者不進，不肖不退，百職廢壞，庶事不從，其過在政教舒緩。」
value.en: Liu Xiang's Wuxing Commentary says: "When a ruler's sight is clouded, he relies on those near at hand; the worthy are not promoted, the unworthy are not dismissed; every office falls into ruin and nothing is properly managed—the fault lies in slack governance and instruction."
value.literal: Liu Xiang's Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When vision is not clear, employing close favorites, the worthy are not advanced, the unworthy are not removed, the hundred offices are ruined, and the myriad affairs are not followed—the fault lies in lax government and teaching.'"

value.zh: 時帝狂躁、荒淫無度之應。
value.en: This was Heaven's response to an emperor's frenzy, recklessness, and boundless debauchery.
value.literal: At that time it was the response of the emperor's frenzy, wildness, and boundless debauchery.

value.zh: 草妖高祖時，上黨有人，宅後每夜有人呼聲，求之不得。
value.en: Grass-spirit omen: During Emperor Gaozu's reign, a man in Shangdang heard voices calling every night behind his house, yet however he searched, he could find no one.
value.literal: Grass demon—during Gaozu's reign, in Shangdang there was a man whose behind his house every night there were voices calling; he searched but could not find them.

value.zh: 去宅一里所，但見人參一本，枝葉峻茂。
value.en: About a li from his home he found only a single ginseng plant, its branches and leaves towering and lush.
value.literal: One li from the house, he only saw one ginseng plant, its branches and leaves luxuriant.

value.zh: 因掘去之，其根五尺餘，具體人狀，呼聲遂絕。
value.en: When he dug it up, the root was more than five chi long and shaped like a human being—and the calling voices stopped.
value.literal: He dug it out; its root was more than five chi, fully in human form, and the calling voices then ceased.

value.zh: 蓋草妖也。
value.en: It was evidently a grass-spirit omen.
value.literal: This was probably a grass demon.

value.zh: 視不明之咎。
value.en: This was the penalty for clouded royal sight.
value.literal: The fault of unclear vision.

value.zh: 時晉王陰有奪宗之計，諂事親要，以求聲譽譖皇太子，高祖惑之。
value.en: At the time the Prince of Jin secretly plotted to seize the succession, fawning on the emperor's intimates and trading on his reputation to slander the crown prince—and Gaozu was taken in.
value.literal: At that time Prince of Jin secretly harbored a plan to seize the succession, flattered those close to the emperor, sought reputation, and slandered the crown prince; Gaozu was deluded by this.

value.zh: 人參不當言，有物憑之。
value.en: Ginseng ought not to speak; some entity had possessed it.
value.literal: Ginseng should not speak; some thing possessed it.

value.zh: 上黨，黨與也。
value.en: Shangdang: dang means "faction."
value.literal: Shangdang—dang means faction.

value.zh: 親要之人，乃党晉王而譖太子。
value.en: The emperor's intimates formed a faction backing the Prince of Jin and defaming the crown prince.
value.literal: Those close to the emperor were a faction for the Prince of Jin and slandered the crown prince.

value.zh: 高祖不悟，聽邪言，廢無辜，有罪用，因此而亂也。
value.en: Gaozu failed to see the truth, heeded slander, deposed the innocent and empowered the guilty—and disorder followed.
value.literal: Gaozu did not understand, listened to evil words, deposed the innocent, employed the guilty, and thereby came disorder.

value.zh: 羽蟲之孽梁中大同元年，邵陵王綸在南徐州，坐廳事。
value.en: Winged-creature calamity: In Liang's Datong year 1, Prince Shaoling Xiao Lun was sitting in his reception hall in Southern Xuzhou.
value.literal: Calamity of winged insects—in the first year of Datong of Liang, Prince of Shaoling Lun was at Southern Xuzhou, seated in the reception hall.

value.zh: 有野鳥如鳶數百，飛屋樑上，彈射不中。
value.en: Several hundred wild birds resembling kites alighted on the roof beams; neither bow nor sling could bring them down.
value.literal: There were several hundred wild birds like kites that flew onto the roof beams; shooting and slinging could not hit them.

value.zh: 俄頃失所在。
value.en: Moments later they disappeared.
value.literal: In a moment they vanished.

value.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「野鳥入君室，其邑虛，君亡之他方。」
value.en: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When wild birds enter the ruler's hall, the city will be emptied and the lord will flee elsewhere."
value.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When wild birds enter the ruler's chamber, the city will be emptied, and the ruler will flee to another region.'"

value.zh: 後綸為湘東王所襲，竟致奔亡，為西魏所殺。
value.en: Later Lun was attacked by the Prince of Xiangdong, fled in defeat, and was killed by Western Wei.
value.literal: Afterward Lun was attacked by the Prince of Xiangdong, and in the end fled and was killed by Western Wei.

value.zh: 陳後主時，有張貴妃、孔貴嬪，並有國色，稱為妖豔。
value.en: During Houzhu's reign Consorts Zhang and Kong, both renowned for beauty, were called bewitchingly lovely.
value.literal: During Chen Houzhu's reign there were Consort Zhang and Consort Kong, both of national beauty, called bewitchingly lovely.

value.zh: 後主惑之，寵冠宮掖，每充侍從，詩酒為娛。
value.en: Houzhu was captivated; they held supreme favor in the palace, always at his side, devoted to poetry and wine.
value.literal: Houzhu was deluded by them; their favor topped the palace; they always attended him; poetry and wine were their pleasure.

value.zh: 一入後庭，數旬不出，荒淫侈靡，莫知紀極。
value.en: Once they entered the inner palace, they did not emerge for weeks; debauchery and extravagance knew no bounds.
value.literal: Once entering the rear palace, for several ten-day periods they did not emerge; debauchery and extravagance beyond measure.

value.zh: 府庫空竭，頭會箕斂，天下怨叛，將士離心。
value.en: The treasury emptied; taxes piled high; the realm rebelled; officers and soldiers lost heart.
value.literal: Treasury emptied; taxes piled high; the realm rebelled; officers and soldiers lost heart.

value.zh: 敵人鼓行而進，莫有死戰之士。
value.en: The enemy marched in formation; none would fight to the death.
value.literal: The enemy marched in formation; none would fight to the death.

value.zh: 女德之咎也。
value.en: This was the fault of female influence.
value.literal: The fault of female virtue.

value.zh: 及敗亡之際，後主與此姬俱投于井，隋師執張貴妃而戮之，以謝江東。
value.en: At the moment of defeat, Houzhu and these consorts threw themselves into a well; Sui forces seized Consort Zhang and executed her to appease Jiangdong.
value.literal: At the moment of defeat and ruin, Houzhu and these consorts together threw themselves into a well; Sui armies seized Consort Zhang and executed her to appease Jiangdong.

value.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「華者，猶榮華容色之象也。
value.en: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Flower symbolizes splendor and beauty.
value.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Flower is the image of splendor and countenance.

value.zh: 以色亂國，故謂華孽。」
value.en: Using beauty to disorder the state—this is called flower calamity."
value.literal: Using beauty to disorder the state—therefore called flower calamity.'

value.zh: 齊後主有寵姬馮小憐，慧而有色，能彈琵琶，尤工歌儛。
value.en: Northern Qi's last emperor had a favored consort Feng Xiaolian—clever and beautiful, skilled on the pipa and especially in song and dance.
value.literal: Northern Qi Houzhu had a favored consort Feng Xiaolian, clever and beautiful, able to play the pipa, especially skilled in song and dance.

value.zh: 後主惑之，拜為淑妃。
value.en: The emperor was captivated and made her Shufei.
value.literal: Houzhu was deluded by her and made her Shufei.

value.zh: 選彩女數千，為之羽從，一女之飾，動費千金。
value.en: Several thousand attendants were selected for her retinue; a single woman's adornments cost a thousand gold pieces.
value.literal: Several thousand colored women were selected as her retinue; one woman's adornment cost a thousand gold.

value.zh: 帝從禽於三堆，而周師大至，邊吏告急，相望於道。
value.en: The emperor was hunting at Sandui when Zhou armies arrived; urgent reports lined the roads.
value.literal: The emperor was hunting at Sandui when Zhou armies arrived in force; border officials reported urgent news one after another on the road.

value.zh: 帝欲班師，小憐意不已，更請合圍。
value.en: The emperor wished to withdraw, but Xiaolian insisted on continuing the hunt.
value.literal: The emperor wished to withdraw the army; Xiaolian was unwilling and asked to continue the encirclement.

value.zh: 帝從之。
value.en: The emperor complied.
value.literal: The emperor followed her.

value.zh: 由是遲留，而晉州遂陷。
value.en: Because of this delay, Jinzhou fell.
value.literal: Because of this delay, Jinzhou then fell.

value.zh: 後與周師相遇于晉州之下，坐小憐而失機者數矣，因而國滅。
value.en: Later, meeting Zhou armies below Jinzhou, he lost opportunity repeatedly because of Xiaolian—and the state was destroyed.
value.literal: Later meeting Zhou armies below Jinzhou, because of Xiaolian he lost opportunity several times, and thus the state perished.

value.zh: 齊之士庶，至今咎之。
value.en: Qi gentry and commoners blame her to this day.
value.literal: The gentry and common people of Qi blame her to this day.

value.zh: 牛禍梁武陵王紀祭城隍神，將烹牛，忽有赤蛇繞牛口，牛禍也。
value.en: Cow omen: Prince Wuling Xiao Ji was sacrificing to the city god; as an ox was about to be cooked, a red snake coiled around its mouth.
value.literal: Cow portent—Prince of Wuling Ji of Liang was sacrificing to the city god; about to cook an ox, suddenly a red snake coiled around the ox's mouth—cow portent.

value.zh: 象類言之，又為龍蛇之孽。
value.en: In symbolic terms, it was also a dragon-and-snake calamity.
value.literal: Speaking in terms of elephant categories, it is also dragon-and-snake calamity.

value.zh: 魯宣公三年，郊牛之口傷，時以為天不享。
value.en: In Lu Duke Xuan's year 3, the suburban ox's mouth was injured; at the time Heaven was thought to reject the offering.
value.literal: In the third year of Duke Xuan of Lu, the suburban ox's mouth was injured; at the time it was thought Heaven did not accept the offering.

value.zh: 棄宣公也。
value.en: Duke Xuan was abandoned by Heaven.
value.literal: Duke Xuan was abandoned.

value.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「逆君道傷，故有龍蛇之孽。」
value.en: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When the ruler's way is violated, dragon-and-snake calamities arise."
value.literal: The Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the ruler's way is violated and injured, therefore there are dragon-and-snake calamities."

value.zh: 是時紀雖以赴援為名，而實妄自尊亢。
value.en: Though nominally going to aid, Ji in fact arrogantly exalted himself.
value.literal: At that time Ji, though nominally going to aid, in fact arrogantly exalted himself.

value.zh: 思心之咎，神不享，君道傷之應。
value.en: The fault of a confused mind; the spirits rejected him—the ruler's way was injured.
value.literal: The fault of the reflective mind; the spirits do not accept; the response of the ruler's way being injured.

value.zh: 果為元帝所敗。
value.en: He was ultimately defeated by Emperor Yuan.
value.literal: In the end he was defeated by Emperor Yuan.

value.zh: 文帝下
value.en: The Annals of Emperor Wen, Part Two
value.literal: Emperor Wen, Part Two

value.zh: 三月，太祖遣大將軍、魏安公尉遲迥率衆伐梁武陵王蕭紀於蜀。
value.en: In the third month Yuwen Tai sent Yuchi Jiong, duke of Wei'an, against Xiao Ji, Liang prince of Wuling, in Shu.
value.literal: In the third month the Grand Duke sent Grand General Duke of Wei'an Yuchi Jiong with troops to campaign against Liang's Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji in Shu.

value.zh: 五月，蕭紀潼州刺史楊乾運以州降，引迥軍向成都。
value.en: In the fifth month Yang Qianyun, Xiao Ji's governor of Tong Province, surrendered and guided Yuchi Jiong toward Chengdu.
value.literal: In the fifth month Xiao Ji's Tong Province governor Yang Qianyun surrendered the province and led Jiong's army toward Chengdu.

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第163卷卷第一百六十三
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 163
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 163, Roll 163

value.zh: 是時，唯荊、益所部尚完實，太尉、益州刺史武陵王紀移告征、鎮，使世子圓照帥兵三萬受湘東王節度。
value.en: At this time only the domains of Jing and Yi remained intact. Grand commandant and Yizhou inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, ordering his heir Yuanzhao to lead thirty thousand men under Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong.
value.literal: At this time only the parts held by Jing and Yi remained intact; Grand Commandant and Yizhou Inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, making his heir Yuanzhao lead thirty thousand men to accept Prince of Xiangdong Yi's command.

value.zh: 圓照軍至巴水，繹授以信州刺史，令屯白帝，未許東下。
value.en: Yuanzhao's army reached the Bashui. Yi made him Xinzhou inspector, ordered him to camp at Baidi, and would not let him march east.
value.literal: Yuanzhao's army reached Bashui; Yi made him Xinzhou Inspector and ordered him to camp at Baidi, not permitting him to go east.

value.zh: 益州沙門孫天英帥徒數千人夜攻州城，武陵王紀與戰，斬之。
value.en: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.
value.literal: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.

value.zh: 黎州民攻刺史張賁，賁棄城走。
value.en: The people of Lizhou attacked inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.
value.literal: The people of Lizhou attacked Inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.

value.zh: 州民引氐酋北益州刺史楊法琛據黎州，命王、賈二姓詣武陵王紀請法琛為刺史。
value.en: The provincials brought in Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi inspector, to hold Lizhou, and sent the Wang and Jia clans to Prince Ji of Wuling to ask that Fachen be made inspector.
value.literal: The provincials brought in the Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi Inspector, to hold Lizhou, and ordered the Wang and Jia clans to go to Prince Ji of Wuling and ask that Fachen be made inspector.

value.zh: 紀深責之，囚法琛質子崇顒、崇虎。
value.en: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.
value.literal: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.

value.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑朔，法琛遣使附魏。
value.en: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.
value.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.

value.zh: 武陵王紀帥諸軍發成都，湘東王繹遣使以書止之曰：「蜀人勇悍，易動難安，弟可鎮之，吾自當滅賊。」
value.en: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him: "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels."
value.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him, saying, "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, you can hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels."

value.zh: 又別紙云：「地擬孫、劉，各安境界；
value.en: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.
value.literal: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.

value.zh: 情深魯、衛，書信恆通。」
value.en: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass."
value.literal: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass."

value.zh: 武陵王紀遣潼州刺史楊乾運、南梁州刺史譙淹合兵二萬討楊法琛，法琛發兵據劍閣以拒之。
value.en: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou inspector Qiao Yan with twenty thousand men to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.
value.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou Inspector Qiao Yan with a combined force of twenty thousand to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.
